subject.title: Runtime context carrier positioned AFTER user message causes severe model confusion and reasoning token waste

question: Should OpenClaw prioritize carrier-before-user semantic ordering by default, retain tail relocation for cache efficiency, or adopt a provider-aware canonical policy after live comparison?
rationale: The current implementation is intentional cache behavior, while the report supplies a model-specific quality and cost concern; source review alone cannot choose the acceptable cross-provider trade-off.

options.title: Run comparison, then prefer semantic ordering
options.body: Collect redacted multi-turn traces and cache/cost measurements on the affected reasoning models, then move the carrier before the active request if the observed quality improvement is repeatable.

options.title: Keep tail relocation
options.body: Retain the cache-oriented order if controlled traces do not show reproducible degradation beyond model-specific prompting behavior.

options.title: Adopt a provider-aware policy
options.body: Use an explicit provider-family policy only if evidence shows materially incompatible behavior that cannot be handled by one stable framing and ordering contract.

recommendation.title: Run comparison, then prefer semantic ordering
recommendation.body: Collect redacted multi-turn traces and cache/cost measurements on the affected reasoning models, then move the carrier before the active request if the observed quality improvement is repeatable.
